WI:SCI.LS1.A.1.cc_advanced: I can compare external parts of several plants and animals and explain how each part helps in daily life.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.1.cc_at_target: I can describe how organisms use their external parts to do daily functions.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.1.cc_approaching: I can name an external part of a plant or animal and say what it does, with help.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.1.cc_emerging: I can point to parts of a plant or animal, such as leaves, legs, or wings.

WI:SCI.LS1.A.4.cc_advanced: I can explain how internal and external structures work together to help an organism survive and reproduce.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants and animals have internal and external structures for growth, survival, behavior, and reproduction.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.4.cc_approaching: I can name an internal or external structure and its job, with a word bank.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.4.cc_emerging: I can name body parts of animals and parts of plants, using pictures.

WI:SCI.LS1.A.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how cells, tissues, and organs work together in a body system using an example.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that living things are made of cells that form tissues and organs specialized for body functions.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.m.cc_approaching: I can put cells, tissues, and organs in order of size, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.m.cc_emerging: I can say that living things are made of cells.

WI:SCI.LS1.A.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how specialized cell systems and feedback keep an organism's internal conditions stable in a new situation.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain how systems of specialized cells perform life functions and how feedback maintains internal conditions.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.h.cc_approaching: I can describe one body system and one feedback example, such as sweating, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.A.h.cc_emerging: I can name body systems and organs, using pictures.

WI:SCI.LS1.B.1.cc_advanced: I can compare how different parents and offspring behave and explain how each behavior helps survival.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.1.cc_at_target: I can describe behaviors of parents and offspring that help the offspring survive.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.1.cc_approaching: I can give one example of a parent animal caring for its young, with help.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.1.cc_emerging: I can match baby animals to their parents, using pictures.

WI:SCI.LS1.B.3.cc_advanced: I can compare life cycles of different organisms and explain what all life cycles have in common.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that reproduction is essential and that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.3.cc_approaching: I can put the stages of one life cycle in order, with picture cards.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.3.cc_emerging: I can say that living things are born and grow, using pictures.

WI:SCI.LS1.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain how behaviors, genes, and environment together affect reproduction and growth.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain how animal behaviors increase reproduction and how genetic and environmental factors affect growth.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.m.cc_approaching: I can give an example of a behavior that helps reproduction and a factor that affects growth, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that living things need food and water to grow.

WI:SCI.LS1.B.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how mitosis and differentiation produce different cell types and what happens when this goes wrong.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that cells grow and divide by mitosis and differentiate into specific cell types.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe the stages of mitosis using a diagram, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that cells divide to make new cells.

WI:SCI.LS1.C.K.cc_advanced: I can explain and compare what different plants and animals need for food and energy.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.K.cc_at_target: I can say that animals get food from plants or other animals and that plants need water and light.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.K.cc_approaching: I can sort animals by what they eat, with picture cards.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.K.cc_emerging: I can say that animals eat and plants need water.

WI:SCI.LS1.C.5.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how plants get most of their material from air and water and how this energy reaches animals.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that food gives animals materials and energy and that plants get material mainly from air and water and energy from sunlight.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.5.cc_approaching: I can describe what plants and animals need to grow, using a diagram and word bank.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.5.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need sunlight and animals need food.

WI:SCI.LS1.C.m.cc_advanced: I can trace energy from sunlight through photosynthesis into food and explain how cells release it.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants use light energy to make sugars and that food is broken down in organisms to release energy.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.m.cc_approaching: I can describe the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis, using a diagram.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.m.cc_emerging: I can say that plants make food using sunlight.

WI:SCI.LS1.C.h.cc_advanced: I can trace atoms and energy from photosynthesis through cellular respiration and into proteins and DNA.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain how molecules from photosynthesis build proteins and DNA and how respiration moves matter and energy through an organism.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how photosynthesis and respiration are linked, using a diagram with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.C.h.cc_emerging: I can name the inputs of photosynthesis and respiration, with a word bank.

WI:SCI.LS1.D.1.cc_advanced: I can explain how animals use several senses and signals to respond and survive, with examples.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.1.cc_at_target: I can describe how animals sense, communicate, and respond with behaviors that help them grow and survive.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.1.cc_approaching: I can give an example of an animal responding to something it senses, with help.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.1.cc_emerging: I can name the senses animals use, such as seeing and hearing.

WI:SCI.LS1.D.4.cc_advanced: I can model how different senses send information to the brain and how memory guides an animal's actions.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that sense receptors detect different information and animals use perceptions and memories to guide actions.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.4.cc_approaching: I can match a sense organ to the information it detects, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.4.cc_emerging: I can name the five senses and their body parts.

WI:SCI.LS1.D.m.cc_advanced: I can explain the full pathway from sense receptor to brain and compare a reflex with a memory.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that sense receptors send signals along nerve cells to the brain, which leads to behavior or memories.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.m.cc_approaching: I can draw the path from a sense organ to the brain, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.m.cc_emerging: I can say that the brain receives messages from the senses.

WI:SCI.LS1.D.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how chemical signals and nerve networks process and store information, using an example such as learning.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that organisms process and store information through specific chemicals and interconnected networks.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.h.cc_approaching: I can describe that nerves and hormones carry messages in the body, with support.
WI:SCI.LS1.D.h.cc_emerging: I can say that the brain and nerves help us respond.

WI:SCI.LS2.A.2.cc_advanced: I can explain how plants and animals depend on each other, using examples of pollination and seed dispersal.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants need water and light and depend on animals for pollination or to move seeds.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.2.cc_approaching: I can describe how a bee or bird helps a plant, with help.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.2.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need water and sunlight.

WI:SCI.LS2.A.5.cc_advanced: I can build a food web and explain how energy from plants reaches all animals and how decomposers recycle materials.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that animals' food traces back to plants and that food webs include producers, consumers, and decomposers.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.5.cc_approaching: I can build a simple food chain starting with a plant, using picture cards.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.5.cc_emerging: I can say what some animals eat.

WI:SCI.LS2.A.m.cc_advanced: I can predict how changing a living or nonliving factor will affect several populations in an ecosystem.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that organisms depend on living and nonliving factors, which can limit growth, and describe competitive, predatory, and helpful interactions.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.m.cc_approaching: I can identify predator, prey, and competition in an ecosystem, with a word bank.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.m.cc_emerging: I can name living and nonliving things in an ecosystem.

WI:SCI.LS2.A.h.cc_advanced: I can use data to explain how biotic and abiotic factors set carrying capacity and predict population changes.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that ecosystems have carrying capacities set by biotic and abiotic factors that affect species abundance.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.h.cc_approaching: I can read a population graph and identify carrying capacity, with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.A.h.cc_emerging: I can say that ecosystems have limited food and space.

WI:SCI.LS2.B.5.cc_advanced: I can model how matter moves between air, soil, and living things and explain the role of decomposers.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that matter cycles between air, soil, and organisms as they live and die.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.5.cc_approaching: I can describe what happens to a dead plant in soil, with help.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.5.cc_emerging: I can say that dead leaves break down into soil.

WI:SCI.LS2.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use a food web model to trace both matter and energy and explain how atoms are reused.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that atoms cycle between living and nonliving parts of ecosystems and food webs show how matter and energy are transferred.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.m.cc_approaching: I can draw a food web with producers, consumers, and decomposers, with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.m.cc_emerging: I can name a producer and a consumer.

WI:SCI.LS2.B.h.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy transfer between trophic levels and explain why there are fewer top predators.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that photosynthesis and respiration power life and only part of the matter and energy moves up a food web.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.h.cc_approaching: I can use an energy pyramid to show energy decreasing at each level, with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.B.h.cc_emerging: I can name the levels of a food chain.

WI:SCI.LS2.C.3.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain what different organisms will do when their environment changes, using evidence.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that when the environment changes, some organisms survive and reproduce, some move, and some die.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.3.cc_approaching: I can describe what happened to one organism when its environment changed, with sentence frames.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.3.cc_emerging: I can say that animals can be harmed when their home changes.

WI:SCI.LS2.C.m.cc_advanced: I can use biodiversity data to judge the health of an ecosystem and predict effects of a disruption.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that ecosystems change over time, disruptions shift populations, and biodiversity measures ecosystem health.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.m.cc_approaching: I can describe how one disruption changed an ecosystem, with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.m.cc_emerging: I can name things that disrupt ecosystems, such as pollution.

WI:SCI.LS2.C.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from a real disturbance to predict whether the ecosystem will recover or change.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that after a disturbance an ecosystem may return to its original state or become a very different ecosystem.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how an ecosystem changed after a disturbance, using a case study with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.C.h.cc_emerging: I can name events that disturb ecosystems.

WI:SCI.LS2.D.3.cc_advanced: I can compare group behaviors of different animals and explain how each helps survival.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that living in a group helps animals get food, defend themselves, and cope with change.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.3.cc_approaching: I can give one example of animals in a group helping each other, with help.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.3.cc_emerging: I can name animals that live in groups.

WI:SCI.LS2.D.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how a loss of biodiversity would affect a specific human resource and ecosystem service.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity affect human resources such as food and medicine and ecosystem services such as clean water.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.m.cc_approaching: I can name a resource people get from nature and how it could be lost, with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.m.cc_emerging: I can say that people get food and water from nature.

WI:SCI.LS2.D.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence for how group behavior increases survival of individuals and their relatives.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that group behavior evolved because it increases survival chances for individuals and their genetic relatives.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.h.cc_approaching: I can describe an example of group behavior and its benefit, with support.
WI:SCI.LS2.D.h.cc_emerging: I can name animals that live in groups.

WI:SCI.LS3.A.1.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how young organisms are like and unlike their parents and other organisms of the same kind.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.1.cc_at_target: I can explain that young organisms are like, but not exactly like, their parents and resemble others of the same kind.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.1.cc_approaching: I can name one way a young animal looks like its parent, with help.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.1.cc_emerging: I can match young animals to their parents.

WI:SCI.LS3.A.3.cc_advanced: I can sort traits into inherited, environmental, or both and justify each choice with evidence.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that many traits are inherited, others come from the environment, and many involve both.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.3.cc_approaching: I can give one inherited trait and one trait caused by the environment, with support.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.3.cc_emerging: I can say that children look like their parents.

WI:SCI.LS3.A.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how a gene's protein leads to a specific trait, using an example.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that genes mainly control specific proteins, which affect an individual's traits.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.m.cc_approaching: I can say that genes carry information for traits, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.m.cc_emerging: I can name some traits, such as eye color.

WI:SCI.LS3.A.h.cc_advanced: I can explain why cells with the same DNA can be different, using gene expression in specific cell types.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that DNA carries instructions for traits and that all cells have the same DNA but express different genes.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.h.cc_approaching: I can describe that DNA is in every cell and carries instructions, with support.
WI:SCI.LS3.A.h.cc_emerging: I can say that DNA is found in cells.

WI:SCI.LS3.B.1.cc_advanced: I can compare variation among individuals of the same kind and explain why they still belong together.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.1.cc_at_target: I can explain that individuals of the same kind of plant or animal are similar but vary in many ways.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.1.cc_approaching: I can name one way two animals of the same kind are different, with help.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.1.cc_emerging: I can point to differences between two animals of the same kind.

WI:SCI.LS3.B.3.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain how both inherited information and environment shape an organism's traits.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that organisms vary because of different inherited information and that the environment also affects traits.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.3.cc_approaching: I can describe how a plant's environment changed its growth, with support.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.3.cc_emerging: I can say that living things of the same kind can look different.

WI:SCI.LS3.B.m.cc_advanced: I can predict variation in offspring and explain how a mutation could be beneficial, harmful, or neutral.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that each parent gives half the genes in sexual reproduction, causing variation, and that mutations can change genetic information.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.m.cc_approaching: I can explain that offspring get genes from both parents, using a diagram.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that babies get traits from both parents.

WI:SCI.LS3.B.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how meiosis, replication errors, and environmental mutations each create variation, with examples.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that trait variation depends on genetic and environmental factors and that genetic variation comes from mutations and meiosis.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe one source of genetic variation, with support.
WI:SCI.LS3.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that people in a population have different traits.

WI:SCI.LS4.A.3.cc_advanced: I can use fossil evidence to describe past organisms and environments and compare them to today.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that fossils give evidence about organisms and environments from long ago and that some living things resemble them.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.3.cc_approaching: I can match a fossil to a living organism it looks like, with help.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.3.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils are remains of old living things.

WI:SCI.LS4.A.m.cc_advanced: I can use fossil and anatomical evidence to infer relationships between organisms and describe changes over time.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that the fossil record and anatomical similarities document change in life forms and allow inference of evolutionary lines.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.m.cc_approaching: I can describe a pattern in the fossil record, with support.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.m.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils show life from long ago.

WI:SCI.LS4.A.h.cc_advanced: I can compare DNA, protein, and anatomical evidence to build and defend a branching tree of relationships.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that lines of descent can be inferred by comparing DNA, amino acid sequences, and anatomical and embryo evidence.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.h.cc_approaching: I can read a simple evolutionary tree and identify close relatives, with support.
WI:SCI.LS4.A.h.cc_emerging: I can say that similar organisms may be related.

WI:SCI.LS4.B.3.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how a specific difference gives some individuals an advantage in a given environment.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that differences between individuals of the same species can give advantages in surviving and reproducing.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.3.cc_approaching: I can describe a trait that helps an animal survive, with sentence frames.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.3.cc_emerging: I can notice differences between animals of the same kind.

WI:SCI.LS4.B.m.cc_advanced: I can compare natural and artificial selection using examples and explain how each changes a population.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural and artificial selection happen when some traits give an advantage, making those traits more common.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.m.cc_approaching: I can give an example of natural or artificial selection, with support.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that farmers choose the best plants or animals to breed.

WI:SCI.LS4.B.h.cc_advanced: I can use data to show how variation and selection pressure change trait frequency over generations.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural selection needs genetic variation and that traits helping survival become more common.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how a helpful trait spreads in a population, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.LS4.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that animals with helpful traits survive better.

WI:SCI.LS4.C.3.cc_advanced: I can explain why a specific organism survives in one environment but not another, using its traits.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that particular organisms can only survive in particular environments.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.3.cc_approaching: I can match an organism to the environment where it lives, with help.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.3.cc_emerging: I can say where some animals live, such as fish in water.

WI:SCI.LS4.C.m.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how a species adapted over generations to a changed environment.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that species change over time as natural selection makes traits suited to a new environment more common.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.m.cc_approaching: I can describe an adaptation and how it helps in an environment, with support.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.m.cc_emerging: I can name an adaptation of an animal.

WI:SCI.LS4.C.h.cc_advanced: I can use the factors of evolution to explain adaptation, speciation, or extinction in a real example.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that evolution results from genetic variation, competition, and better survival and reproduction, causing adaptation.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.h.cc_approaching: I can name the main factors of evolution and give an example, with a graphic organizer.
WI:SCI.LS4.C.h.cc_emerging: I can say that species can change over a long time.

WI:SCI.LS4.D.2.cc_advanced: I can compare the variety of living things in two habitats and explain why they differ.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that there are many kinds of living things in any area, living in different places on land and in water.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.2.cc_approaching: I can name living things found on land and in water, with help.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.2.cc_emerging: I can sort animals into land and water animals.

WI:SCI.LS4.D.3.cc_advanced: I can predict how a habitat change would affect several populations and explain why.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that populations live in many habitats and that habitat change affects the organisms living there.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.3.cc_approaching: I can describe how one habitat change affected an animal, with sentence frames.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.3.cc_emerging: I can name different habitats, such as desert and ocean.

WI:SCI.LS4.D.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how a biodiversity change in a specific ecosystem affects human resources and services.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that changes in biodiversity influence human resources and the ecosystem services people rely on.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.m.cc_approaching: I can name one ecosystem service, such as clean water, and how it depends on biodiversity, with support.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.m.cc_emerging: I can say that people depend on plants and animals.

WI:SCI.LS4.D.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how human actions increase or reduce biodiversity and propose ways to sustain it.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that biodiversity increases with new species and decreases with extinction and that humans depend on and affect it.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.h.cc_approaching: I can describe one way humans harm biodiversity and one way they protect it, with support.
WI:SCI.LS4.D.h.cc_emerging: I can say what biodiversity means, with a picture.
